reason: Complex graph parsing and GPU interaction; high risk of memory corruption in GPU process.
Direct access to file system operations; historical source of sandbox escapes.
Exposes direct raw byte communication with Bluetooth devices; high risk of firmware exploitation and Bluetooth stack vulnerabilities.
Bypasses standard network stack security checks; allows arbitrary TCP connections.
Exposes complex on-device AI model interaction to renderers; high risk of resource exhaustion and model parsing vulnerabilities in privileged service.
Interacts with OS share sheet and handles file attachments; high risk of file handling vulnerabilities and interaction with external apps.
Allows renderer to register Blob URLs; potential for URL spoofing and XSS if renderer can control the URL.
Allows renderer to send arbitrary USB control requests; high risk of device firmware exploitation.
Allows renderer to send arbitrary HID reports; high risk of device firmware exploitation.
Allows renderer to write arbitrary data to serial ports; high risk of interaction with attached hardware.
Allows renderer to send arbitrary MIDI data including SysEx; high risk of device exploitation and bypassing OS MIDI protections.
Exposes privileged printing path and triggers PDF parsing from the renderer; risk of memory exhaustion and parsing vulnerabilities.
Exposes complex accessibility tree parsing to the Screen AI service; high risk of parsing vulnerabilities in the ML service.
Allows renderer to write arbitrary data with arbitrary format names to the system clipboard; high risk of exploiting vulnerabilities in native applications that read the clipboard.
Part of Captured Surface Control; allows a renderer to send wheel events to a captured tab, potentially interacting with privileged or cross-origin content.
Vulnerable to cross-site cache poisoning in unlocked process models and exposes deserialization attack surface.
Exposes complex audio parsing and processing in the browser to untrusted renderer content.

Allows renderer to register blobs backed by arbitrary file paths. Although checked against child process security policy, it relies on complex permission validation and potentially legacy unsafe patterns (`FromUnsafeValue`).
Exposes creation of Shared Storage worklets; high complexity in cross-origin data handling and interaction with Fenced Frames, representing a significant attack surface in the privacy sandbox.
Allows renderer to send arbitrary commands directly to the smart card reader driver (IFD Handler); high risk of driver exploitation and interaction with system components.
Allows renderer to send arbitrary APDUs to smart cards; high risk of card applet exploitation, bypassing PINs, or interacting with secure elements.
